planting.note: Plant rhizome cuttings horizontally 2-3 inches deep in spring in moist, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Cluster climbs vigorously and needs a strong trellis or arbor at least 12-15 feet tall. Only female plants produce usable cones.

directions: Plant rhizomes horizontally in moist, fertile, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun to partial shade; provide a tall, sturdy support for the vigorous climbing bine. Cluster is the oldest surviving American hop cultivar, an heirloom variety of unclear original parentage that dominated US hop production for much of the 19th and early 20th centuries before newer aroma hops took over, and it remains valued today for its clean, mild, slightly spicy and floral character and reliable, disease-resistant vigor. The vine dies to the ground each fall and re-emerges rapidly each spring to climb 15-20 feet on strings or a trellis; harvest the soft green cones in late summer when papery, fragrant, and sticky with lupulin resin, then dry promptly for brewing or storage. Like other hops, Cluster performs best in cool-summer climates with long day length, and struggles with the sustained heat and humidity of zone 8-9 Gulf South summers, so give it the coolest, best-ventilated site available and expect a lighter cone yield than in traditional hop-growing regions.

directions: Plant rhizomes horizontally in moist, fertile, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun to partial shade; provide a tall, sturdy support for the vigorous climbing bine. Fuggle is a classic English hop cultivar dating to the late 19th century, long the backbone of traditional English bitters and other cask ales, prized for its mild, earthy, woody, and slightly minty aroma that defines the classic English hop character as distinctly as Cascade defines American craft brewing. The vine dies to the ground each fall and re-emerges rapidly each spring, climbing 15-20 feet on strings or a trellis; cones ripen in late summer and should be picked when papery, aromatic, and sticky with lupulin, then dried promptly for use. Fuggle prefers a cool, temperate, long-day growing season and struggles with the intense heat and humidity of Gulf South summers, so site it in the coolest, most open-air spot available and expect reduced yield and cone quality compared to traditional English or Pacific Northwest production.

planting.note: Plant rhizome cuttings horizontally 2-3 inches deep in spring in moist, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Zeus climbs vigorously and needs a strong trellis or arbor at least 12-15 feet tall. Only female plants produce usable cones.

directions: Plant rhizomes horizontally in moist, fertile, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun to partial shade; provide a tall, sturdy support for the vigorous climbing bine. Zeus (also sold as Columbus/Tomahawk/Zeus, or CTZ) is a high-alpha-acid American bittering hop developed for efficient, potent bitterness in a wide range of beer styles, with a pungent, slightly herbal and resinous aroma alongside its primary role as a bittering rather than aroma hop. The vine dies to the ground each fall and re-emerges vigorously each spring, climbing 15-20 feet on strings or a trellis; because its high alpha-acid content delivers strong bitterness from a relatively small harvest, even a modest home planting can supply a meaningful amount of bittering hops for brewing. Harvest cones in late summer when papery, fragrant, and sticky with lupulin resin, then dry promptly. Like other hops, Zeus prefers a cool, long-day growing season and performs poorly through the sustained heat and humidity of Gulf South summers, so give it the coolest, most open site available and expect a lighter yield than in traditional hop-growing regions.
